sentences: Bits 0–1 of the FSSM input record's flags byte (byte 7; `fssm_header.read_methods`) give the **read method** of each table position: bit 0 (0x01) = read through `v_interp_mov_f32`, bit 1 (0x02) = read through `v_interp_p1/p2` or the f16 forms.
They do not give the D3D interpolation mode, which is PSV0's (row "PS interpolation modes", `tools/ps_interp_modes.py`, #1256).
Exactly one bit is set in every corpus record (bit 1 in 51,191, bit 0 in 4,600).

In all 12,101 PS every bit-0 position the code reads is read only by `v_interp_mov_f32` (4,295 read positions), every bit-1 position only by `p1/p2` or the f16 forms (49,594), and no position is read both ways (1,902 positions are unread, and 88 reads fall past the table).
The translator follows the read method, which is what the code does: `v_interp_mov` → `Flat`, `p1/p2` → a plain input (perspective, pixel center; `BaryCoordKHR` for raw i/j).
That this one pair is perspective-center holds because PSV0 lists no centroid, sample or noperspective generic input, and the code reads one barycentric pair (#1256).

Table positions don't pair one-to-one with PSV0 rows, since the table keeps only the inputs the compiled code uses, so a PSV0 row's mode and the record's read method can differ at a paired position; #1256 counts those cases.

`rdna2spirv.check_read_methods` refuses a PS whose read position disagrees with its record's read method (`v_interp_mov` of a bit-1 position, `p1/p2`/f16 of a bit-0 one), or whose record has neither or both bits, instead of reading it as perspective-center.
It refuses 0 of 12,101 PS, and shard 0/12 translates byte-identically to before the check.

GPU-checked by @Vonsek on #1246 (RTX 5080 and Radeon integrated graphics, stock `ps_flat` with a hand-built table of read methods 2 and 1): the smooth channels match a per-center perspective reference, the flat channel keeps the provoking value, and flipping either record's read method makes the translator refuse the shader.
Bit 3 (0x08, 11,619 records) is a Float16-typed parameter per #1256.
